title: Bus-stop upgrades recorded in mixed units

blocks.text: A city's transit agency ranks bus-stop upgrades by three measures: rider time saved, complaints avoided and operating savings. The data comes from three teams, and each records amounts in the unit it likes: rider time in minutes or hours, complaints one by one or by the dozen, savings in dollars or thousands of dollars. Every amount arrives as a pair `(amount, unit)`, and so does each measure's reference, the swing the agency's board agreed on. `UNITS` and `in_base` (given) say what each unit measures and how many base units it is.

Write `score(benefit, reference, weights)` in `stops.py`: the weighted sum, over the measures, of the benefit as a share of its reference. Then write `rank(projects, reference, weights)`, the project names from the highest score to the lowest, with equal scores in name order so that the list is the same on every run.

A team switching from hours to minutes, or the board restating a reference in dollars instead of $k, has not changed anyone's mind about any project, so it must not change any score. About eight lines.

cases.says: a project's score is worked out by hand from its benefits, the references and the weights
four projects are ranked from the highest score to the lowest
a benefit recorded in minutes or dollars instead of hours or $k scores the same
the references restated in other units give the same scores and the same ranking
projects with equal scores are listed in name order

origin.section: A Normalized Score Divides by a Reference, So the Units Cancel

concepts: dividing by a reference in the same unit gives a score with no unit
